title: Capturing Quality of Life and Priorities for Clinical Research in Parents and Patients With Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
official: Capturing Quality of Life and Priorities for Clinical Research in Parents and Patients With Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
summary:
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in childhood is a significant burden and reduces the quality of life for both children and their parents. CKD is especially burdensome when it progresses to end stage kidney disease (ESKD, previously referred to as end-stage renal disease or ESRD), placing considerable demands on a childs entire family. Although studies are available for all-cause CKD and for some disease subsets, there is no study capturing quality of life in children or adolescents specifically affected by autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). These children are often severely affected prenatally and postnatally have problems due to massive kidney enlargement, hypertension, kidney failure, and portal hypertension. They often need to receive kidney replacement therapy during childhood.

The need to include patients and their lived experience in the design of clinical trials exists for all diseases, but is implemented infrequently, especially in the field of rare diseases. The negative consequences of limited patient/parent input in clinical trial design for rare diseases has been recently highlighted by a report from the International Rare Diseases Research Consortium (IRDiRC).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Subjects should be over 18 years of age and permanently live in the same household as the child/ young person with ARPKD.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Insufficient understanding of the questions due to intellectual capabilities or language barriers. However, translation by a professional interpreter is permissible.

Lack of written informed consent. Subjects that choose not to have their responses recorded.
